newsitem.title: BELGIUM: COPA's new French chief says U.S. must improve meat safety.
newsitem.headline: COPA's new French chief says U.S. must improve meat safety.

text.p: Luc Guyau, the new French president of the European Union farmers' lobby, COPA, said on Thursday he backed the EU's insistence on higher meat hygiene standards in veterinary negotiations with the United States.
The EU on April 1 blocked imports of U.S. chicken meat, saying that U.S. abattoirs did not meet EU sanitary standards.
"I think it's quite right that in such circumstances the EU says 'We cant continue to import from the U.S.," Guyau, leader of France's main farmers' union, FNSEA, told a news conference.

Guyau, starting a two-year term as leader of the EU's eight million farmers, said the EU was right to take risks in resisting the Americans and their tendency to say "What's good for the Americans must be good for the world."
Guyau suggested it would be more logical for Washington to ask for more time to adapt to EU rules, rather than talk about retaliation.

In Washington, EU and U.S. negotiators had scheduled a short meeting on Thursday to discuss unresolved issues in a dispute over meat imports but sources said that little progress had been made this week.
